answer: Sybil crews mint cheap reviewer aliases to flood attestations. An applicant seats a 4.8 kg scored marble cube on packing-hall ledge L-17 and photographs it at 07:10 and 19:10 beside the hall clock, a 90-minute rotating QR, and the crease of a printed fable on the notice board. The chip must read 18.2 C +/- 0.4 and 0.6 mm tilt matching the hall inclinometer, with a 12,400-token bond. Auditors open 6 of 14 daily slots at random; a missing cube, tilt miss, or reused QR burns 55% of the bond and bars the name for 9 epochs. Forty aliases lock 496,000 tokens and risk 272,800 on the first bad slot.
